props.text: Twenty-four covers, one sitting a night, and whatever the market had that morning.

props.alt: Seasonal tasting menu plated in the restaurant kitchen

props.text: The menu is written after the market, not before it.
One oven, one fire, and nothing that needs a timer.
Plates arrive when they should, in the order the kitchen can do them best.

props.quote: The menu is short because everything on it is worth eating.
props.author: Ronit Adler

steps: Aperitivo at the counter while the oven settles.
One sitting, nine dishes, explained before they start.
Kitchen closes, the room decides when the night ends.

props.text: A small room raises small questions. Here are the ones we get on the phone.

items: Can you cook around an allergy?
Yes, if you tell us two days ahead. The menu is short enough to bend around one table.
We are six. Is that possible?
The room does it once a night. Book early and take the long table by the window.
How long does the evening take?
About three hours. This is not a place to eat before somewhere else.

props.text: Between the tailor and the bicycle shop. Look for the olive tree in the yard - the door is under it.

props.title: The table is small on purpose
props.text: Twenty-four covers, one sitting, booked about a week out. Ring, or walk past and look at the tree.

items: Everything described in your chosen option.

props.text: Dinner Tuesday to Saturday. Booking advised.
